# cron-expression-parser

> Zero-dependency 5-field cron parser with precise validation errors, nextRun/nextN UTC scheduling, and describe() human sentences.

cron-expression-parser parses standard 5-field cron expressions (minute
hour day-of-month month day-of-week) — ranges, steps, lists, and
JAN-DEC/SUN-SAT names — with field-specific error messages on invalid
input, computes the next matching run time(s) in UTC (bounded
minute-by-minute search, documented, no infinite loops), and renders a
human-readable description of a schedule.

## API

- `parse(expr: string): CronExpression` — throws `CronParseError` on invalid input.
- `validate(expr: string): { valid: boolean; errors: string[] }`
- `matches(date: Date, exprOrCron: string | CronExpression): boolean`
- `nextRun(exprOrCron: string | CronExpression, from?: Date): Date` — UTC, bounded ~4yr search.
- `nextN(exprOrCron: string | CronExpression, n: number, from?: Date): Date[]`
- `describe(exprOrCron: string | CronExpression): string` — e.g. "every 15 minutes", "at 09:00 on weekdays".
- `class CronParseError extends Error`
- `interface CronExpression { minute: FieldSpec; hour: FieldSpec; dayOfMonth: FieldSpec; month: FieldSpec; dayOfWeek: FieldSpec; raw: string }`
- `interface FieldSpec { values: Set<number>; isWildcard: boolean; raw: string }`

All scheduling is UTC only — no DST handling (see README).

## Install

```bash
npm install cron-expression-parser
```

Part of the Ferrow open-source toolkit: https://github.com/Ruzylo-cloud/ferrow-toolkit — sponsored by https://ferrow.ai
